properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued September 27 at 6:00PM EDT until September 28 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal Ocean.

* WHEN...Until 2 PM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Back bay flooding may persist beyond
Monday afternoon.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal
flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued September 27 at 4:18PM AST until September 29 at 6:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT..Life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...Beaches of northern Puerto Rico, from Aguadilla through
Fajardo.

* WHEN...Monday morning through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued September 27 at 12:18PM PDT until September 28 at 5:00AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and breaking waves due to elevated surf. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. For the High
Surf Advisory, breaking waves of 4 to 7 feet with dangerous
rip currents.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Focused
across exposed south facing coasts.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through 5 AM Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory and High Surf Advisory, from 5
AM Monday to 5 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate to locally significant beach
erosion is likely. Very localized damage possible to most
vulnerable areas. There is an increased risk for ocean
drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to
sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Areas of most concern are Avalon, Long
Beach (Peninsula and Belmont Shore). While the surf will likely
be smaller than Marie (from earlier this month), the lingering
erosion effects enhance the vulnerabilities for locally more
significant coastal flooding.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or

beach erosion is possible.

stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

* WHEN...Until Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 12.5 feet, Water affects old U.S. Highway 61 near the
river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM CDT Sunday the stage was 12.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
Thursday morning and continue falling to 8.8 feet Sunday, October
04.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

The next statement will be issued by Monday morning.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 27 at 7:48AM MDT until September 29 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible across
much of central and southern Utah between Monday morning and early
Tuesday morning.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country, Central Mountains, San Rafael Swell, Bryce Canyon Country,
Capitol Reef National Park and Vicinity, Glen Canyon Recreation
Area/Lake Powell, South Central Utah, Southern Mountains, Upper
Sevier River Valleys, Western Canyonlands, Lower Washington County
and Zion National Park.

* WHEN...From Monday morning through early Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn scars
including Cottonwood, Widemouth 2, France Canyon, Monroe Canyon,
Forsyth, and Silver King.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Deep moisture originating from tropical systems in the Eastern
Pacific draws into portions of central and southern Utah on
Monday. Concurrently, an upper-level system traversing the Desert
Southwest will result in ample instability that will produce
widespread heavy rainfall across the area. Isolated heavier
storms will be capable of producing rainfall rates in excess of 1
inch per hour at times.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor remains within Minor Flood Stage and is
actively cresting due to an ongoing period of northerly winds and
tidal effects. River levels are forecast to gradually subside through
Minor Flood Stage this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Sunday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Sunday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to crest around 2.7 feet today.
The river is then forecast to slowly subside through Minor Flood
Stage this week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 2.6
feet on 10/14/1996.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued September 27 at 2:25AM EDT until September 28 at 3:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and rough surf with breaking waves
of 3 to 6 feet.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive and long duration rainfall.

* WHERE...All of northern and central Arizona.

* WHEN...From Sunday evening through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding will be possible over burn areas, low-water
crossings, creeks, streams, washes and swimming holes. Larger
creeks and rivers may exceed bankfull. Flooding of paved roads and
highway underpasses will be possible. Unpaved roads could become
muddy and impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Low pressure will interact with tropical moisture from the
eastern Pacific. This could potentially produce numerous showers
and embedded thunderstorms, with heavy rain that will fall over
saturated soils and burn scars. This could lead to localized
flash flooding and rises on local rivers, such as the Little
Colorado River.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
